short: The octamer ATGCAAAT is the site read by the 16 human POU-domain factors, including OCT1/POU2F1, OCT2/POU2F2, PIT1/POU1F1, the BRN2/BRN1 group (POU3F1-4), the BRN3 group (POU4F1-3) and OCT4/POU5F1. What makes the family unusual is the binding unit: a POU-specific domain and a homeodomain joined by a flexible linker, so the two halves of the site can be re-arranged. The same proteins therefore also form dimers on the PORE and MORE elements and sit next to SOX partners in the SOX-OCT composite elements that control pluripotency genes. Hits matter because octamer elements drive immunoglobulin and snRNA promoters and because OCT4 occupancy of SOX-OCT sites is a defining feature of pluripotent cells. The motif is short and AT-rich, so it is common.
long:
## The factors

Sixteen human POU genes fall into six classes: POU1F1 (PIT1), POU2F1-3 (OCT1, OCT2, OCT11/SKN-1a), POU3F1-4 (OCT6, BRN2, BRN1, BRN4), POU4F1-3 (BRN3A/B/C), POU5F1 (OCT4) together with the retrogene-derived POU5F1B locus, and POU6F1/2. All of them use one composite DNA-binding unit, described from sequence in 1988 and named after PIT1, OCT1, OCT2 and *C. elegans* UNC-86: an N-terminal POU-specific domain (POU-S), a four-helix bundle whose helix-turn-helix resembles the bacteriophage lambda and 434 repressors, tethered by a flexible 15-27 residue linker to a C-terminal POU-homeodomain (POU-HD), a conventional 60-residue three-helix homeodomain. Expression is class-restricted. POU2F1 is essentially ubiquitous; POU2F2 is lymphoid; POU5F1 is confined to pluripotent and germ cells; POU3F and POU4F members mark defined neural, retinal and inner-ear lineages; POU1F1 is restricted to the anterior pituitary.

## The motif

The core is the 8-bp octamer ATGCAAAT, first noted as a conserved element upstream of immunoglobulin genes. The 1994 crystal structure of the OCT1 POU domain on an octamer site showed why the site is bipartite: POU-S grips the 5' ATGCA half and POU-HD the 3' AAAT half, the two domains bind opposite faces of the duplex, and the linker is disordered and contacts no bases. The 3' half is a TAAT-type homeodomain site read in the reverse orientation; POU-S contributes most of the base-specific contacts, which is why the ATGC block is the least tolerant part of the site. Because the linker tethers rather than spaces, the half-sites can be rearranged: two POU domains dimerize on the PORE (ATTTGAAATGCAAAT) or on the MORE (ATGCATATGCAT) using two non-overlapping surface patches, and only the PORE arrangement recruits the coactivator OBF-1/POU2AF1. Pooled across JASPAR, HOCOMOCO, CIS-BP and the Vierstra archetypes, this family's consensus is tTATGCaAATt - the octamer plus its usual flanking T - but cohesion is only 0.68, because many HT-SELEX models for POU3F, POU4F and POU6F members report homeodomain-half arrangements (TGCATAAT, ATTAATTATGCA, TAATTA, TCATTA) instead of the full octamer. Those are configuration variants of one binding unit, not separate specificities.

## Where it acts

Octamer sites are classically promoter-proximal, in immunoglobulin heavy- and light-chain promoters, the histone H2B promoter and snRNA promoters. The best-characterized POU enhancer elements are composite: an OCT4 octamer immediately adjacent to a SOX HMG site. OCT4 and SOX2 dimerize in different relative orientations on the FGF4 and UTF1 enhancers, and it is the arrangement of the two boxes in the DNA, not a switch in the proteins, that sets the geometry. The Vierstra archetype set recovers POU5F/NANOG and POU2F/POU3F clusters, reflecting how routinely these sites are found with partner motifs. Because the octamer is only 8 bp and AT-rich, an exact match is expected on the order of 10^5 times in 3.1 Gb, so the great majority of matches are unoccupied in any one cell type; occupancy tracks which POU class is expressed. Methyl-SELEX places several POU factors among those whose affinity is changed by CpG methylation in flanking positions, although the octamer core itself has no CpG.

## Biology and disease

POU5F1/OCT4 maintains the pluripotent state and is one of the four factors that reprogram human fibroblasts to induced pluripotent stem cells. POU2F2 with OBF-1 drives immunoglobulin promoter activity in B cells, and the PORE-versus-MORE distinction is the structural explanation for that coactivator dependence. POU3F2 and POU3F3 pattern the neocortex; POU4F1-3 specify sensory neurons, retinal ganglion cells and inner-ear hair cells; POU1F1 controls the growth hormone and prolactin genes. Mendelian loss of POU1F1 causes combined pituitary hormone deficiency, and mutations in POU3F4 and POU4F3 cause X-linked and autosomal dominant deafness respectively. In cancer, POU2F3 defines a tuft-cell-like subtype of small-cell lung carcinoma, and POU5F1 is re-expressed in germ cell tumors.

## Reading a hit

A good octamer match tells you that a POU factor could bind; it does not tell you which one. The in vitro models for POU2F1, POU2F2, POU2F3, POU3F1-4 and POU5F1 are all the same 8-9 bp, so treat a hit as "POU family" unless expression data narrow it. Do not read a bare TAATTA or TCATTA match as POU: that is the homeodomain half alone and is shared with most of the homeodomain superfamily, which is exactly why two low-information CIS-BP and Vierstra entries in this family have nearest neighbours in the HOX and Q50 groups. Conversely, a full PORE, MORE or SOX-OCT composite is much stronger evidence, because the spacing constraint is specific. HOCOMOCO ids are informative here: PO2F1.H14CORE.0.PS.A and PO5F1.H14CORE.2.SM.B carry in vitro (S/M) support, whereas the P-only models such as PO3F2.H14CORE.0.P.B come from ChIP alone and may reflect co-binding.
caveats: A hit identifies the POU family, not a paralogue: the octamer models for OCT1, OCT2, OCT4 and the BRN proteins are interchangeable at 8-9 bp. The family is only moderately cohesive (0.68) because HT-SELEX returns several linker configurations, and the lowest-information members reduce to TAAT cores indistinguishable from the rest of the homeodomain superfamily; three entries here have nearest neighbours in other homeodomain families. ChIP-derived (P-grade) POU models can capture partner motifs, particularly SOX sites in pluripotent cells. Exact octamers occur roughly 10^5 times genome-wide, so a match alone is weak evidence without expression or footprint support.
